blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The corridor runs on King George Boulevard from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River, about 7 kilometres and about 490 hectares (1,210 acres), with Highway 99 to the east, the Nicomekl River to the north and 8 Avenue to the south.
This is the south segment only: the same road continues through Newton to Surrey City Centre, but the City plan area, and this page, stop at the Nicomekl River.

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Detached houses here sit in a corridor the City planned for mixed development type and density, parks and trails, a transportation network and engineering infrastructure — not as a single subdivision.

At the north end, land at 3600 King George Boulevard is zoned General Agriculture Zone (A-1) and lies in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), so the corridor's detached stock includes acreage-edge lots beside farmland, not only urban lots.

The south end, between 16 Avenue and 24 Avenue, falls under the Semiahmoo Town Centre Plan as well as the corridor plan, so houses there sit beside the town-centre density the corridor plan alone does not describe.

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The city-wide Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH), secondary suite and Zoning By-law No. 12000 rules apply here as across Surrey; the corridor-specific point is that A-1 / ALR lots at the Nicomekl end, such as 3600 King George Boulevard, are treated as agricultural land in the City report, not as ordinary urban house lots.

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The corridor is about 7 kilometres long but has no City-stated west boundary road, so two houses both described as “King George Corridor” can sit well apart, near 8 Avenue or near the Nicomekl River.
Highway 99, not a local street, is the plan area's east border, so east-side corridor houses back toward a provincial highway corridor rather than a neighbourhood street.
The Semiahmoo Town Centre Plan overlaps only the 16 Avenue to 24 Avenue stretch, so school, shopping and density expectations differ between the corridor's south end and its Nicomekl end.

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Nicomekl Riverfront Park, Oxbow Zone Phase 1 — 3600 King George Boulevard; applicant City of Surrey; Application No. 7925-0403-00 proposes amending the King George Corridor plan to redesignate about 6.2 hectares bounded by the Nicomekl River, King George Boulevard and Winter Crescent from Golf Course, Commercial and Landscape Buffer to Park; status: planning report dated February 9, 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: getting around

items.t: Highway 99 is the corridor's east edge and Highway 10 (56 Avenue / 58 Avenue corridor) is reached north of the Nicomekl River crossing — the plan page itself names only Highway 99, the river and 8 Avenue as borders.

blocks.text: King George Corridor Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status for lots near 3600 King George Boulevard: the City report for that site states the site falls within the ALR and is zoned A-1, which limits non-farm uses.

blocks.text: King George Corridor home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

71 houses sold in King George Corridor with a median price of $1,345,000 (the middle half sold between $1,179,950 and $1,515,000), taking a median of 21 days to sell at 96.7% of the last list price; 15% sold above list. They had a median $561 per square foot, a median year built of 1988 and a median lot of 7,155 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in King George Corridor?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 84 houses listed in King George Corridor. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is King George Corridor a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in King George Corridor had a sales ratio of 4%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in King George Corridor from June to October 2026?
faq.a: King George Corridor accounted for 42 of the 294 houses sold across South Surrey and White Rock from June to October 2026.

faq.q: Is a King George Corridor house in Newton or South Surrey?
faq.a: South Surrey, on this page. The City plan area runs from 8 Avenue to the Nicomekl River, bordered by Highway 99 to the east. King George Boulevard continues north through Newton to City Centre, but that northern stretch is outside this plan area and outside this page, so check which side of the Nicomekl River a listing sits on before comparing houses.

faq.q: Can I rely on the old King George Corridor plan for what can be built?
faq.a: No. The planning process completed in 1995 produced a land use and development concept plan, but the City states those designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update, and Council endorsed updated designations in Corporate Report R246 on December 2, 2024. Use the current OCP designation for the specific lot.

faq.q: Does the corridor have rapid transit now?
faq.a: Not on this south segment. TransLink's R1 RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard only between Newton Exchange and Guildford Exchange, north of the Nicomekl River.

faq.q: What did houses in King George Corridor sell for?
faq.a: The median house sale in King George Corridor was $1,345,000, across 71 sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in King George Corridor?
faq.a: Half sold in 21 days or less, at a median 96.7% of the last list price; 15% went over asking (sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
